load_card_overreach: short-term overreach is OK; plan recovery.
load_card_high_risk: sharp load spike; elevated injury/illness risk.
load_card_acute_help: Average daily training load over the last 7 days. "Load" is Edwards' TRIMP — time in each HR zone weighted by zone intensity (1× for Z1 up to 5× for Z5). Higher = more recent stress on the body.
load_card_chronic_help: Average daily training load over the last 28 days. Represents the fitness base you've built up — a higher chronic load means your body is adapted to handle more work.
load_card_acwr_help: Acute : Chronic Workload Ratio — acute (7d) divided by chronic (28d). The 0.8–1.3 band is the sweet spot for productive adaptation. Above 1.5 is a sharp spike with elevated injury risk.
load_card_monotony_help: How uniform your training intensity has been over the last 7 days (mean ÷ standard deviation of daily load). Above 2.0 is concerning — too many same-effort sessions limit adaptation. Mix easy and hard days.
load_card_weekly_delta_aria: What is the weekly load delta?
load_card_weekly_delta_help: Percent change in total weekly load versus the previous week. Jumps above +25% or drops below −25% compound the ACWR signal — sustainable progression is typically within ±10%.
load_card_short_history: Less than 28 days of history is available — chronic load and ACWR will sharpen as more activities sync.

help_revision: GymCraft writes the rest of this week again, from today. Sessions you did or edited stay as they are. Use it when you are ill or tired, or after you missed a key session. Each rewrite uses one revision from your monthly limit. A failed rewrite does not count.

help_budget: The recovery budget is the most training load this week must carry. GymCraft sets it from your load in the last 28 days when it writes the week. More load than the budget increases the risk of fatigue and injury.
help_pull: GymCraft writes one week at a time, so each week fits how your training went. Tell it how next week looks, then write the week. This does not use a revision.
help_recut: A recut lays out the plan again from the next week that is not written. Use it when your race date moves or you want a different school. Written weeks stay as they are.
help_checkin: Tell GymCraft how you feel each day. After poor or ill days, it offers to rewrite the rest of the week easier.

school_polarized_lore: Seiler found that endurance athletes everywhere train about 80 % easy and 20 % hard. Fitzgerald turned it into plans: most runs truly easy, a few truly hard, and very little in between.
school_polarized_phase_aerobic_loss: Fewer weeks of 80/20 training means less aerobic base on race day.
school_daniels_tagline: Precise paces from your race result.
school_daniels_lore: Jack Daniels coached Olympians and wrote the Running Formula. Every pace comes from your race result through his VDOT tables, and every week is built around two quality days.
school_daniels_phase_fi_intent: Easy mileage and strides to build resilience.
school_daniels_phase_fi_loss: Without Foundation there is no easy weeks to absorb the quality work.
school_daniels_phase_eq_loss: Without Early Quality there is no repetition work to build speed and economy.
school_daniels_phase_tq_loss: Without Transition Quality there is no interval weeks to raise your VO2max.
school_daniels_key_q1_reason: Quality day: the session this phase is built around.
school_daniels_key_q2_reason: Quality day: the session this phase is built around.
school_daniels_key_long_reason: The L run holds the week together.
school_pfitzinger_tagline: High mileage and threshold work, built for the marathon.
school_pfitzinger_lore: Pete Pfitzinger ran two Olympic marathons and wrote Advanced Marathoning. His plans pile up mileage, a medium-long run and weekly lactate-threshold work, all paced from your threshold.
school_pfitzinger_phase_endurance_intent: Build mileage and the long run.
school_pfitzinger_phase_endurance_loss: Fewer Endurance weeks means less mileage under you before the threshold work starts.
school_pfitzinger_phase_lt_intent: Threshold volume on top of endurance.
school_pfitzinger_phase_lt_loss: Fewer threshold weeks means a lower lactate threshold and a slower marathon pace.
school_pfitzinger_phase_race_prep_loss: Fewer Race Preparation weeks means less VO2max work and fewer tune-up races.
school_pfitzinger_phase_taper_loss: A shorter taper means reaching the start line less fresh.
school_pfitzinger_key_long_reason: Pfitzinger calls the long run "number one".
school_pfitzinger_key_lt_reason: The weekly LT session is the cornerstone workout.
school_pfitzinger_key_medium_long_reason: The second endurance run of the week.
school_pfitzinger_key_vo2_reason: Race Preparation is built around it.

mk_seo_title: GymCraft™ — AI workout plans & Garmin running analytics
mk_seo_description: AI-generated workout plans synced to your Garmin, plus training-load analytics and weekly AI reports for every run you record. Free to start.
mk_hero_sub: GymCraft builds your workout plans, syncs them to your Garmin, and turns every session you record into training-load analytics and coach-style weekly reports
mk_target_heading: The fastest way to target your training and get the results you want
mk_target_p1: Training plans are built around [[individual fitness levels, goals, and body types,]] so every exercise contributes directly to achieving specific results. This tailored approach maximizes efficiency and effectiveness.
mk_target_p2: Whether the goal is [[weight loss, muscle gain, endurance, or recovery]], a custom plan adjusts exercises, intensity, and progression rates according to the user’s unique goals, allowing for steady progress.
mk_target_p3: The plan is only half the picture. GymCraft also reads the sessions you actually record, turns them into [[training load]], and tells you whether the work is adding up the way you intended — so you can adjust from [[evidence rather than guesswork]].
mk_img_garmin_alt: AI fitness app connected to Garmin
mk_img_gym_alt: AI personal coach - generate workout plan and send to Garmin with one click
mk_time_p1: With a personalized plan, every workout session is designed to make the most of the time available. Don't waste time on [[unnecessary exercises]] or [[aimless routines]].
mk_time_p2: By following a plan specifically crafted to your needs, you can reach your goals more quickly, reducing time spent on ineffective or irrelevant exercises.
mk_time_p3: Tailored plans can accommodate [[busy lifestyles]], allowing for [[flexibility]] in workout duration and frequency to fit the user's schedule.
mk_who_beginners: If you're new to working out and don’t have a specific training plan yet, our app is the perfect [[starting point]]. It helps guide you through effective, goal-oriented workouts tailored to your fitness level, allowing you to build a [[strong foundation]] and stay motivated with a clear path forward.
mk_who_advanced_title: Advanced sport enthusiasts seeking new challenges
mk_who_advanced: For those with more experience, our app serves as a valuable [[source of inspiration]]. It provides fresh workout ideas and exercises you might not have considered, helping you break through plateaus, [[diversify your training]], and push your limits further.
mk_who_runners_title: Runners who want to know if it's working
mk_who_runners: You already record every session. GymCraft turns that history into [[training load]], tells you whether you're building or [[heading for trouble]], and reviews your week the way a coach would — using your own data rather than a generic template.
mk_who_trainers_title: Personal trainers in need of a head start
mk_who_trainers: Personal trainers can use the app to quickly generate a base training plan skeleton for their clients. The app saves time by providing a [[well-structured starting point]], which trainers can further customize and expand, or use it to [[discover new exercises and programming ideas]] that enhance their clients' routines.
mk_garmin_p_before: Effortlessly sync your AI-generated workout plans with your
mk_garmin_p_after: account. With just a click, send your personalized routines directly to your Garmin device and stay on track wherever you train.
mk_garmin_li2: Export training plans in one step
mk_garmin_li3: Access workouts on your Garmin watch or app
mk_garmin_li4: Track progress and adapt plans in real time
mk_garmin_claim: Check out the first AI powered fitness workout plan generator with direct Garmin integration.
mk_running_p: Sync your Garmin activities and get a full picture of your training. GymCraft turns every session you record into a training load, compares your last 7 days against your last 28, and tells you whether you're building fitness or digging a hole.
mk_running_li1: Training load, ACWR and monotony, with a plain-English status
mk_running_li2: Every sport counts toward load — runs, rides, swims and hikes
mk_running_li3: 7-day distance broken out per sport, never mixed together
mk_running_li4: Coach-style weekly AI reports with recommended adjustments
mk_running_li5: Ask AI about any single run, split by split
mk_running_claim: Stop guessing whether you're overdoing it — read it off the numbers your watch already collected.
mk_keep_heading: What should you keep in mind?
mk_keep_sub: The training plan is just one component
mk_keep_p: To get the desired training results, in addition to the right training plan, there are several important elements to keep in mind:
mk_how1: User enters details on current health status, training level, goals and available equipment
mk_how2: App builds a prompt based on user data and guidelines for creating plans
mk_how3: App sends prepared prompt to the generative AI model which crafts a training plan
mk_how4: The generated plan is processed and formatted to be delivered to the user in its final form
mk_tc_consistency_d: Consistently following the training plan and adhering to nutritional guidelines is essential for progress
mk_tc_technique_d: Proper form ensures that force is evenly distributed across muscles and joints, reducing injury risk
mk_tc_recovery_d: Rest and recovery are crucial for muscle repair, preventing injury, and overall performance
mk_tc_nutrition_d: Proper nutrition fuels workouts, aids recovery, and supports muscle growth or fat loss

mk_faq1_a: Yes. The free tier lets you generate AI workout plans, connect your Garmin account and sync your activities, and gives you {reports} AI weekly reports a month plus {explains} run explanation a day. The number of gym plans a free account can generate is capped.
mk_faq2_a: There is an optional Supporter tier — €4 a month or €36 a year. It raises the AI limits to {reports} weekly reports and {plans} gym plans a month plus {explains} run explanations a day, uses a more capable AI model, extends the Garmin history import from {freeDays} to {days} days, and unlocks report export. GymCraft is a hobby project — the tier exists to cover its running costs, not to lock away the basics.
mk_faq3_q: Do I need a Garmin watch?
mk_faq3_a: Not for the gym side — AI workout plans work without any device. Running analytics does need a Garmin account, because GymCraft reads the activities you have already recorded from Garmin Connect. Other platforms are not supported yet.
mk_faq4_q: Do my rides and swims count, or only runs?
mk_faq4_a: They count. Training load is calculated from every activity you record — runs, rides, swims, hikes — because cardiovascular stress accumulates regardless of the sport. Distance is a different matter: it is reported per sport and never added together, since a kilometre swum is not a kilometre run.
mk_faq5_q: What is training load and ACWR?
mk_faq5_a: Every activity is turned into a TRIMP score from your heart rate and how long you trained. ACWR compares the average daily load of your last 7 days against your last 28 — your recent work against the base you have built. Ramp up too quickly and GymCraft flags the risk before you feel it.
mk_faq6_q: Which AI model does GymCraft use?
mk_faq6_a: GymCraft runs on OpenAI models. Free accounts use a fast, cost-efficient model; Supporters get the more capable one for weekly reports and run analysis. Models are upgraded as better ones ship.
mk_faq7_a: Yes. Training-load analytics, coach-style weekly AI reports and Garmin activity sync are the most recent additions. New features land regularly, and the free tier gets them too.
